label: Formulated the selfobject concept and the bipolar self supported by mirroring and idealization
description: Heinz Kohut formulated the selfobject as an indispensable psychic function sustaining the structural cohesion and vitality of the self.
historicalContext: Developed in 'The Analysis of the Self' (1971) and formalized in 'The Restoration of the Self' (1977).
dialecticalTension: Narcissism is not an infantile phase to be outgrown, but an autonomous lifelong developmental necessity.

label: Overturned Freud's theory of primary narcissism, positing two separate, parallel developmental lines
description: Kohut broke with Freud's drive-discharge view of narcissism as an obstacle to object love, establishing Self Psychology.
historicalContext: Kohut presented his breakthrough paper 'Forms and Transformations of Narcissism' in 1966.
dialecticalTension: Freud's economic hydraulic drive model versus Kohut's phenomenological immersion through vicarious introspection (empathy).

label: Contested Kernberg on the etiology of narcissism: developmental arrest versus defensive rage structure
description: Kohut and Kernberg engaged in a legendary controversy regarding the nature and clinical treatment of narcissistic personality disorder.
historicalContext: The Kohut-Kernberg debates dominated American psychoanalytic symposiums and journals throughout the 1970s and 1980s.
dialecticalTension: Kohut's empathetic mirroring of a fragile arrested self versus Kernberg's confrontation of split-off grandiose defenses and underlying oral rage.
